{{nihongo|'''Mononobe Shrine'''|物部神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Echigo Province]].

{{commons category|Category:Mononobe-jinja (Kashiwazaki)}}
[[ja:物部神社 (柏崎市)]]

{{wikidata link|Q17219569|commons|Category:Mononobe-jinja (Kashiwazaki)|ja|物部神社 (柏崎市)|check_date=2026-05-18}}

== Overview ==
[[File:Mononobe-jinja (Kashiwazaki) torii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Torii]]
'''Mononobe Shrine''' (もののべじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|lt=Shinto shrine|lt_ja=神社}} at Futada (ふただ), {{ill|Nishiyama, Niigata|ja|西山町 (新潟県)|lt=Nishiyama|lt_ja=西山町}}, {{ill|Kashiwazaki, Niigata|ja|柏崎市|lt=Kashiwazaki|lt_ja=柏崎市}}, {{ill|Niigata Prefecture|ja|新潟県|lt=Niigata Prefecture|lt_ja=新潟県}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha|lt_ja=式内社}} (small) and the {{ill|Ichinomiya|ja|一宮|lt=ninomiya|lt_ja=二宮}} of {{ill|Echigo Province|ja|越後国|lt=Echigo Province|lt_ja=越後国}}; under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|lt=former shrine ranking system|lt_ja=旧社格}} it was a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|lt=prefectural shrine|lt_ja=県社}}. It is also called Futada Mononobe Shrine and Futada Shrine. The main sanctuary is a three-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造|lt=nagare-zukuri|lt_ja=流造}} building, and the shrine's founding date is unknown.

=== Deities ===
The shrine has three deities.{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Nihon no Kamigami)|1985|p=396–399}}{{Sfn|Essa no Jinja|2002|p=46–47}}

'''Principal deity'''
* '''Futata no Amenomononobe no Mikoto''' (二田天物部命, ふたたのあめのもののべのみこと)
*: In the "Tenjin Hongi"<ref group="original">''Sendai Kuji Hongi'', "Tenjin Hongi". – [{{NDLDC|991097/120}} ''Kokushi Taikei'' vol. 7] (Keizai Zasshisha, 1897–1901), National Diet Library Digital Collection, frames 120–121.</ref> of the ''{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi|ja|先代旧事本紀|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi|lt_ja=先代旧事本紀}}'', "Futata Mononobe" heads the list of the "twenty-five groups of Heavenly Mononobe" who attended {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|lt=Nigihayahi|lt_ja=饒速日命}} when he descended from heaven.{{Sfn|Essa no Jinja|2002|p=46–47}} In the "Tenson Hongi"<ref group="original">''Sendai Kuji Hongi'', "Tenson Hongi". – [{{NDLDC|991097/145}} ''Kokushi Taikei'' vol. 7] (Keizai Zasshisha, 1897–1901), National Diet Library Digital Collection, frame 145.</ref> {{ill|Umashimaji|ja|宇摩志麻治命|lt=Umashimaji|lt_ja=宇摩志麻治命}} leads the "Heavenly Mononobe" to subdue the rebels.{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Nihon no Kamigami)|1985|p=396–399}}
*: The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku|lt_ja=新撰姓氏録}}'' ({{ill|Kōnin (era)|ja|弘仁|lt=Kōnin|lt_ja=弘仁}} 6, {{ill|815|ja|815年|lt=815|lt_ja=815年}}) lists "Futata Mononobe" among the unclassified families of the Right Capital, as "descendants of Futata no Amenomononobe, attendant of Kamu-Nigihayahi when he descended".{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Nihon no Kamigami)|1985|p=396–399}}{{Sfn|Essa no Jinja|2002|p=46–47}}
*: The ''{{ill|Shintōshū|ja|神道集|lt=Shintōshū|lt_ja=神道集}}'' gives his {{ill|Honji suijaku|ja|本地垂迹説|lt=honji butsu|lt_ja=本地仏}} as {{ill|Amitābha|ja|阿弥陀如来|lt=Amida|lt_ja=阿弥陀如来}}.{{Sfn|Chūsei Shokoku Ichinomiya-sei|2000|p=369}}

'''Secondary deities'''
* Mononobe no Chizakura no Mikoto (物部稚桜命, もののべちざくらのみこと): deity of the Wakamiya Shrine, merged here in {{ill|Meiji era|ja|明治|lt=Meiji|lt_ja=明治}} 40 ({{ill|1907|ja|1907年|lt=1907|lt_ja=1907年}}).
* {{ill|Takeminakata|ja|タケミナカタ|lt=Takeminakata no Mikoto|lt_ja=健御名方命}} (たけみなかたのみこと): deity of the Suwa Shrine, merged here in Meiji 40 (1907).

The ''Echigo Yashi'' gives the deity as {{ill|Umashimaji|ja|宇摩志麻治命|lt=Umashimaji|lt_ja=宇摩志麻治命}}, but the ''{{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|ja|特選神名牒|lt=Tokusen Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=特選神名牒}}'' calls this a forced connection and holds Futata no Amenomononobe to be correct.{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Nihon no Kamigami)|1985|p=396–399}}

== History ==
=== Founding and tradition ===
According to the shrine's tradition (the Edo-period ''Futada-gū Denki''), the deity Futata no Amenomononobe came to {{ill|Koshi Province|ja|越国|lt=Koshi|lt_ja=高志国}} in attendance on {{ill|Ame-no-Kaguyama|ja|天香山命|lt=Ame-no-Kaguyama|lt_ja=天香語山命}}, the deity of {{ill|Yahiko Shrine|ja|彌彦神社|lt=Yahiko Shrine|lt_ja=彌彦神社}}, the {{ill|Ichinomiya|ja|一宮|lt=ichinomiya|lt_ja=一宮}} of Echigo.{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Nihon no Kamigami)|1985|p=396–399}} After parting from Ame-no-Kaguyama at Ishiji (now Ishiji, Nishiyama, Kashiwazaki), someone offered him two rice fields (''futa-da'') at Takisaka, so he settled there and named the village "Futada".{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Nihon no Kamigami)|1985|p=396–399}} He is said to have been buried on the high mound of Hanyūda in Futada.{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Nihon no Kamigami)|1985|p=396–399}}

Tradition also says the shrine moved several times:{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Nihon no Kamigami)|1985|p=396–399}}
* In the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇|lt=Emperor Sujin|lt_ja=崇神天皇}}, his twelfth-generation descendant Mononobe no Chizakura moved the shrine from Ishiji beach to Minami-Ōsaki, and the hill where his boat landed was named Funaoka-yama.
* In the reign of {{ill|Empress Suiko|ja|推古天皇|lt=Empress Suiko|lt_ja=推古天皇}} (593–628), to the slope of Mount Kameoka.
* In the {{ill|Jinki|ja|神亀|lt=Jinki|lt_ja=神亀}} era (724–729), to Hanyūda hill.
* In the {{ill|Kōnin (era)|ja|弘仁|lt=Kōnin|lt_ja=弘仁}} era (810–824), to the summit of Mount Kameoka.
* In {{ill|Tennin|ja|天仁|lt=Tennin|lt_ja=天仁}} 1 (1108), to the present site at the foot of Mount Kameoka.
The old site on Mount Kameoka appears on a map of the {{ill|Meitoku|ja|明徳|lt=Meitoku|lt_ja=明徳}} era (1390–1393), which shows many halls large and small on the way up to the inner shrine on the summit.{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Nihon no Kamigami)|1985|p=396–399}}

=== Outline ===
Tradition says that in {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|lt=Enryaku|lt_ja=延暦}} 14 (795) {{ill|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|ja|坂上田村麻呂|lt=Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|lt_ja=坂上田村麻呂}} prayed here and made {{ill|Santō District, Niigata|ja|三島郡 (新潟県)|lt=Santō District|lt_ja=三島郡}} the shrine's domain.{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}

In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳}} of the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|lt=Engishiki|lt_ja=延喜式}}'', completed in {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長 (日本)|lt=Enchō|lt_ja=延長}} 5 (927), it is listed as "Mononobe Shrine" in Santō District, Echigo Province, as a Shikinaisha.{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}} In documents of the ''insei'' period it appears as "Futada-sha", and the proprietor of the province held the right to appoint its chief priest.{{Sfn|Chūsei Shokoku Ichinomiya-sei|2000|p=369}}

Its later course is unknown. In the {{ill|Middle Ages|ja|中世|lt=medieval period|lt_ja=中世}} the ''{{ill|Shintōshū|ja|神道集|lt=Shintōshū|lt_ja=神道集}}'' says "the Ninomiya is called Ryōden Daibosatsu, also Hanyūkoku Daimyōjin".{{Sfn|Chūsei Shokoku Ichinomiya-sei|2000|p=369}} "Ryōden" (両田, "both fields") is "Futada" (二田), and from this the shrine is held to have been the ''ninomiya'' of Echigo.{{Sfn|Chūsei Shokoku Ichinomiya-sei|2000|p=369}} Its rank as ''ninomiya'' is also seen in sworn oaths from the sixteenth century on, which name "Yahiko Daimyōjin and Futada Daimyōjin" together, pairing it with the ''ichinomiya'' {{ill|Yahiko Shrine|ja|彌彦神社|lt=Yahiko Shrine|lt_ja=彌彦神社}} ({{ill|Yahiko, Niigata|ja|弥彦村|lt=Yahiko|lt_ja=弥彦村}}, {{ill|Nishikanbara District, Niigata|ja|西蒲原郡|lt=Nishikanbara District|lt_ja=西蒲原郡}}).{{Sfn|Chūsei Shokoku Ichinomiya-sei|2000|p=369}} The ''Shintōshū''{{'}}s "also Hanyūkoku Daimyōjin" connects with the tradition, mentioned above, that the deity was buried on Hanyūda hill.{{Sfn|Chūsei Shokoku Ichinomiya-sei|2000|p=369}}

In {{ill|Daiei (era)|ja|大永|lt=Daiei|lt_ja=大永}} 6 (1526) the twelfth shogun of the {{ill|Ashikaga shogunate|ja|室町幕府|lt=Ashikaga shogunate|lt_ja=室町幕府}}, {{ill|Ashikaga Yoshiharu|ja|足利義晴|lt=Ashikaga Yoshiharu|lt_ja=足利義晴}}, granted the shrine 3,500 ''kan'' in Santō District as domain, but this was confiscated in the {{ill|Tenshō (Azuchi–Momoyama period)|ja|天正|lt=Tenshō|lt_ja=天正}} era (1573–1592).{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}} In Tenshō 10 (1582) {{ill|Uesugi Kagekatsu|ja|上杉景勝|lt=Uesugi Kagekatsu|lt_ja=上杉景勝}}, who ruled the area, donated a total of 1,070 ''koku'' from six surrounding villages, but the shrine declined when Kagekatsu moved to Aizu in {{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長|lt=Keichō|lt_ja=慶長}} 3 (1598).{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}} In Keichō 16 (1611) it received 50 ''koku'' from {{ill|Matsudaira Tadateru|ja|松平忠輝|lt=Matsudaira Tadateru|lt_ja=松平忠輝}}, newly come to Echigo, and in {{ill|Keian|ja|慶安|lt=Keian|lt_ja=慶安}} 1 (1648) the third shogun of the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|江戸幕府|lt=Tokugawa shogunate|lt_ja=江戸幕府}}, {{ill|Tokugawa Iemitsu|ja|徳川家光|lt=Tokugawa Iemitsu|lt_ja=徳川家光}}, fixed its ''shuinchi'' at 50 ''koku''.{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}

Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|lt=modern shrine ranking system|lt_ja=近代社格制度}} it was made a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|lt=village shrine|lt_ja=村社}} in Meiji 4 (1871), and was raised to {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|lt=prefectural shrine|lt_ja=県社}} in {{ill|Taishō|ja|大正|lt=Taishō|lt_ja=大正}} 12 (1923).{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Nihon no Kamigami)|1985|p=396–399}} In Meiji 40 (1907) the Wakamiya Shrine and the Suwa Shrine were merged into it.{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}

=== Priests ===
The priests are the Mishima family, said to descend from the Futata Mononobe, one of the "five Mononobe" who attended Nigihayahi's descent from heaven.{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Nihon no Kamigami)|1985|p=396–399}}

== Grounds ==
[[File:Mononobe-jinja (Kashiwazaki) honden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Honden (prefectural cultural property)]]
The {{ill|Honden|ja|本殿|lt=honden|lt_ja=本殿}} is a three-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造|lt=nagare-zukuri|lt_ja=流造}} building roofed with pantiles.<ref name="board"/> It is thought to date from the late {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|lt=Muromachi period|lt_ja=室町時代}}, around the late fifteenth century.<ref name="board"/> It once stood on its own, but a ''heiden'' is now joined to its front, and the ''kōhai'' (front porch) has been closed in with board walls.<ref name="board"/> Because the decoration of its tie-beams closely resembles that of the Atago-dō of Raikō-ji in {{ill|Tōkamachi|ja|十日町市|lt=Tōkamachi|lt_ja=十日町市}} (built 1713), the porch is thought to have been altered at that time.<ref name="board"/> The honden is designated a cultural property of Niigata Prefecture.<ref name="board"/>

The grounds also hold a monument to the Tenmei-era ''gimin'' (peasant martyrs).{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}

== Festivals ==
The {{ill|Reisai|ja|例祭|lt=Reisai|lt_ja=例祭}} is held twice a year, on 9 April (spring) and 14 September (great autumn festival).

Special rites include:{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Nihon no Kamigami)|1985|p=396–399}}
* Oyumi-hajime-sai (御弓始祭, 7 February)
*: Before the ''kinensai'', following the story that the deity pacified the land, wild animals of the hills are shot at and a good harvest is prayed for.
* Sakaero-sai (栄呂祭, さかえろさい, 9 March)
*: Worshippers jump, chanting "sakaero, sakaero" ("prosper, prosper") to pray for the parishioners' prosperity. If the voices reach the Minohi Shrine in Kariwa village, the harvest will be good.
* Shinkō-sai (神幸祭, first Day of the Hare of the third month)
*: On the eve, a lion head and a Sarutahiko mask are brought to the chief priest's house; the next day a ceremony is held and the procession goes round the village.
* Hatsuho-kō-sai (初穂講祭, 23 November)
*: Rice offerings are received and thanks given for the new grain.

== Cultural properties ==
=== Niigata Prefecture designated ===
* Tangible cultural properties<ref>[https://www.city.kashiwazaki.lg.jp/soshikiichiran/kyoikuiinkai/hakubutsukan/1/23/3/4282.html Cultural properties of Kashiwazaki (prefecture-designated)] (Kashiwazaki City website).</ref>
** Honden (building)
**: Designated 28 March 1986.
** Two sutra chests inscribed Ōei 15 (craft)
**: Designated 26 March 2024.<ref>Niigata Prefecture Gazette, 26 March 2024, {{PDFlink|[https://kenpo.pref.niigata.lg.jp/bn/R06_03/0326_t23/t23_20240326i29254.pdf Niigata Prefecture Notice no. 348]}} (Niigata Prefecture website).</ref>
** Pair of wooden {{ill|Komainu|ja|狛犬|lt=komainu|lt_ja=狛犬}} (sculpture)
**: Komainu thought to be of the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|lt=Muromachi period|lt_ja=室町時代}}.<ref name="board"/> Made of {{ill|Cercidiphyllum japonicum|ja|カツラ|lt=katsura|lt_ja=桂}} wood; the open-mouthed figure is 62 cm tall and the closed-mouthed one 60 cm.<ref name="board">Information board in the shrine grounds.</ref> They have Muromachi features such as a long throat, a shallow chest and a narrow face, and from their material and construction are thought to have been made locally.<ref name="board"/> Designated 9 March 1973.

=== Kashiwazaki City designated ===
* Tangible cultural properties<ref>[https://www.city.kashiwazaki.lg.jp/soshikiichiran/kyoikuiinkai/hakubutsukan/1/23/3/4275.html Cultural properties of Kashiwazaki (city-designated: buildings, sculpture, crafts)], [https://www.city.kashiwazaki.lg.jp/soshikiichiran/kyoikuiinkai/hakubutsukan/1/23/3/4281.html (calligraphy, documents, paintings)] (Kashiwazaki City website).</ref>
** The shrine's ''Daihannya Haramitta-kyō'' (calligraphy): 443 scrolls.{{Sfn|Essa no Jinja|2002|p=46–47}} Designated 1 September 1969.
** The shrine's printed ''Gobu Daijō-kyō'' (calligraphy): 157 scrolls.{{Sfn|Essa no Jinja|2002|p=46–47}} Designated 1 September 1969.
** Old map of Mononobe Shrine (document): designated 1 September 1969.
** Ancient plan of Mononobe Shrine (document): designated 1 September 1969.
** Vermilion-seal letters of the Tokugawa shoguns for the shrine's lands (early modern documents): designated 1 September 1969.
* Intangible cultural properties<ref>[https://www.city.kashiwazaki.lg.jp/soshikiichiran/kyoikuiinkai/hakubutsukan/1/23/3/4280.html Cultural properties of Kashiwazaki (city-designated: archaeology, historical materials, folk performing arts)] (Kashiwazaki City website).</ref>
** The shrine's ''tayū-mai'' dance: designated 12 June 1980.
* Historic sites<ref>[https://www.city.kashiwazaki.lg.jp/soshikiichiran/kyoikuiinkai/hakubutsukan/1/23/3/4283.html Cultural properties of Kashiwazaki (city-designated: historic sites, natural monuments, places of scenic beauty)] (Kashiwazaki City website).</ref>
** Futada Castle ruins: designated 1 September 1969.
The "Chinese chest for the shrine's dedicated sutras" was designated a Kashiwazaki City tangible cultural property on 1 September 1969; it is now a Niigata Prefecture tangible cultural property.

=== Futada Castle ===
On Mount Takizawa behind the shrine are the ruins of a castle called "Futada Castle",{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Nihon no Kamigami)|1985|p=396–399}} designated a historic site of Kashiwazaki as the "Futada Castle ruins".

The castle was first built by the shrine's priests as "Nagahashi Castle" to guard the shrine lands; later, when {{ill|Suda Nagayoshi|ja|須田長義|lt=Suda Nagayoshi|lt_ja=須田長義}}, a commander of the {{ill|Uesugi clan|ja|上杉氏|lt=Uesugi|lt_ja=上杉家}}, moved there, he renamed it "Kariya Castle".{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Nihon no Kamigami)|1985|p=396–399}} His son Suda Nagashige is said to have moved to Mitsuyama Castle, but the dates of all of this are unknown.{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Nihon no Kamigami)|1985|p=396–399}} Other documents give Motoi Genba-no-kami as lord of the castle.{{Sfn|Mononobe Shrine (Nihon no Kamigami)|1985|p=396–399}}

== Visiting ==
'''Address'''
* 602 Futada, Nishiyama-chō, {{ill|Kashiwazaki, Niigata|ja|柏崎市|lt=Kashiwazaki|lt_ja=柏崎市}}, {{ill|Niigata Prefecture|ja|新潟県|lt=Niigata Prefecture|lt_ja=新潟県}}

'''Access'''
* Nearest station: {{ill|Raihai Station|ja|礼拝駅|lt=Raihai Station|lt_ja=礼拝駅}} on the {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|ja|東日本旅客鉄道|lt=JR|lt_ja=JR}} {{ill|Echigo Line|ja|越後線|lt=Echigo Line|lt_ja=越後線}} (about 16 minutes on foot).
** The place name Raihai ("worship") comes from a worship hall of Mononobe Shrine that stood there.
